provisioned_save_read_only.location: Connection editor → Bottom of form: red error shown when Save is clicked on a connection that was preconfigured from a provisioning file or SQLLY_CONNECTION_ environment variable; explains it is read-only and how to change or copy it.

proxy_host_label.location: Connection editor → Tunnel / Proxy section → Proxy first hop: label above the proxy server host name input, shown after “Use a proxy first hop” is checked.

proxy_host_required.value: O host do proxy é obrigatório
proxy_host_required.location: Connection editor → Tunnel / Proxy section (also Tunnel Profiles dialog) → Validation errors: red error line shown when Save or Test Connection is clicked, when “Use a proxy first hop” is checked but the Proxy host field is empty.

proxy_kind_label.location: Connection editor → Tunnel / Proxy section → Proxy first hop: label above the dropdown choosing the proxy protocol (SOCKS5 or HTTP CONNECT), shown after “Use a proxy first hop” is checked.

proxy_password_label.location: Connection editor → Tunnel / Proxy section → Proxy first hop: label above the masked proxy password input, last field of the proxy settings.

proxy_password_placeholder.location: Connection editor → Tunnel / Proxy section → Proxy first hop → Proxy password field: masked placeholder in the empty input, lowercase noun.

proxy_port_invalid.value: A porta do proxy deve ser 1–65535
proxy_port_invalid.location: Connection editor → Tunnel / Proxy section (also Tunnel Profiles dialog) → Validation errors: red error line shown when Save or Test Connection is clicked, when the Proxy port field is not a number from 1 to 65535.

proxy_port_label.location: Connection editor → Tunnel / Proxy section → Proxy first hop: label above the proxy port input (defaults to 1080), below Proxy host.

proxy_read_only.value: Estas conexões são configuradas no servidor pelo qual o SQLLY é executado e são somente leitura aqui. Peça ao seu administrador para adicionar ou alterar uma.
proxy_read_only.location: Connection editor (View Connection) → Top of form: notice banner shown when SQLLY runs in a browser through a company server whose connections are managed there, explaining the form cannot be edited.

proxy_save_read_only.value: Estas conexões são configuradas no servidor pelo qual o SQLLY é executado e são somente leitura aqui. Peça ao seu administrador para adicionar ou alterar uma.
proxy_save_read_only.location: Connection editor (View Connection) → Bottom of form: red error shown if saving is attempted while connections are managed by the server SQLLY runs through in the browser; explains the form is read-only.

proxy_user_label.location: Connection editor → Tunnel / Proxy section → Proxy first hop: label above the proxy user name input, below Proxy port; optional unless a proxy password is set.

proxy_username_required.value: O nome de usuário do proxy é necessário quando uma senha é definida
proxy_username_required.location: Connection editor → Tunnel / Proxy section (also Tunnel Profiles dialog) → Validation errors: red error line shown when Save or Test Connection is clicked, when a proxy password was entered but the Proxy user field is empty.

redis_cluster_auto.location: Connection editor → Redis options → Cluster mode dropdown: default option that detects automatically whether the Redis server is a cluster.

redis_cluster_enabled.location: Connection editor → Redis options → Cluster mode dropdown: option that always connects in Redis Cluster mode (noun “cluster”).

redis_cluster_mode_label.value: Modo de cluster (vários hosts iniciais podem ser listados no Servidor, separados por vírgula)
redis_cluster_mode_label.location: Connection editor → Redis options (Redis-family engines only): label above the Cluster mode dropdown (Auto / Standalone / Cluster), noting that several seed hosts may be typed comma-separated in the Server field.

redis_cluster_relay_note.value: Através de túneis SSH ou de um proxy, cada nó do cluster é discado por meio do próprio encaminhamento. Uma conexão roteada por retransmissão alcança apenas o nó inicial, por isso o modo cluster não está disponível nesse caso.
redis_cluster_relay_note.location: Connection editor → Redis options: dimmed note under the Cluster node map field explaining that cluster mode works through SSH or a proxy, but not when the connection is routed through a relay device.

redis_cluster_standalone.location: Connection editor → Redis options → Cluster mode dropdown: option that treats the server as a single, non-clustered Redis instance.

redis_entra_host_hint.value: Faz login no Azure Cache para Redis ou no Azure Managed Redis com o ID do objeto da conta e um token Microsoft Entra, atualizado antes de expirar. Os nomes de host terminam em .redis.cache.windows.net ou .redis.azure.net; o TLS é obrigatório (porta 6380 ou 10000). Escolha uma conta conectada abaixo.
redis_entra_host_hint.location: Connection editor → Authentication section: dimmed hint for Redis with Microsoft Entra sign-in, shown when the Server is empty or an Azure Redis host; explains how the Entra token sign-in works. Keep the host suffixes unchanged.

redis_entra_non_azure_host_hint.value: O login do Microsoft Entra funciona apenas com o Azure Cache para Redis e o Azure Managed Redis, cujos nomes de host terminam em .redis.cache.windows.net ou .redis.azure.net — este host não é um deles. Escolha uma conta conectada abaixo.
redis_entra_non_azure_host_hint.location: Connection editor → Authentication section: dimmed warning for Redis with Microsoft Entra sign-in, shown instead of the usual hint when the Server is not an Azure Redis host name. Keep the host suffixes unchanged.

redis_key_delimiter_label.value: Delimitadores de chave (o navegador de chaves agrupa os nomes por eles; vários são permitidos, por exemplo :| — em branco = :)
redis_key_delimiter_label.location: Connection editor → Redis options (Redis-family engines only): label above the key delimiter input; the Redis key browser groups key names into folders on these characters (several may be typed, e.g. :| or space-separated tokens), colon when blank.

redis_node_map_invalid.location: Connection editor → Validation errors: red error line at the bottom of the form shown when Save or Test Connection is clicked, when a line in the Redis Cluster node map cannot be parsed; {error} is the parser detail naming the bad line.

redis_node_map_label.value: Mapa de nós do cluster (endereço anunciado => endereço para conexão; para NAT, mapeamentos de portas ou nós atrás de SSH)
redis_node_map_label.location: Connection editor → Redis options: label above the multi-line Cluster node map box that rewrites each address a cluster node advertises to the address SQLLY should actually dial (NAT, port mapping, SSH).

redis_node_map_placeholder.value: 10.0.0.5:7001 => 127.0.0.1:17001 (um por linha; em branco = usar os endereços que os nós anunciam)
redis_node_map_placeholder.location: Connection editor → Redis options → Cluster node map box: placeholder showing an example mapping line, one mapping per line, blank to dial the advertised addresses; keep the example addresses and “=>” as is.

redis_user_label.location: Connection editor → Authentication section: label above the optional Redis user name input, shown for Redis when Microsoft Entra sign-in is selected (for an access policy naming the identity).

redis_user_placeholder.value: em branco: o ID do objeto do token
redis_user_placeholder.location: Connection editor → Authentication section → Redis user field: placeholder saying that when left blank the Entra token's object id is used as the Redis user name.

relay_authorize_button.location: Connection editor → Routing section → Relay device picker: button beside the “not authorized yet” hint, shown when the selected relay device is not yet paired; pairs this computer with that device.

relay_authorize_failed.location: Connection editor → Routing section: relay error message shown when authorizing (pairing) the selected relay device fails; {error} is the server or network error detail.

relay_authorized.location: Connection editor → Routing section → Relay device picker: dimmed status text under the device dropdown, shown when the selected relay device is already paired with this account (next to the Revoke… button on desktop).

relay_device_not_registered.value: Este dispositivo ainda não está registrado em sua conta.
relay_device_not_registered.location: Connection editor → Routing section: relay error shown when Authorize is clicked but this computer has no device registration on the signed-in SQLLY account, so it cannot be paired.

relay_device_placeholder.location: Connection editor → Routing section → Relay device dropdown: placeholder shown before any relay device is chosen, after “Route through a relay device” is checked.

relay_device_required.value: Selecione um dispositivo de retransmissão para rotear.
relay_device_required.location: Connection editor → Validation errors: red error line at the bottom of the form shown when Save or Test Connection is clicked, when “Route through a relay device” is checked but no relay device is selected in the dropdown.

relay_device_unauthorized.value: Este dispositivo de retransmissão ainda não está autorizado – emparelhe-o antes de rotear.
relay_device_unauthorized.location: Connection editor → Validation errors: red error line at the bottom of the form shown when Save or Test Connection is clicked, when “Route through a relay device” is checked and the selected relay device has not been paired (authorized) yet.

relay_devices_load_failed.value: Não foi possível carregar os dispositivos de retransmissão: {error}
relay_devices_load_failed.location: Connection editor → Routing section: dimmed status text shown in place of the relay controls when the list of relay devices could not be loaded or a relay action failed; {error} is the detail.

relay_devices_loading.location: Connection editor → Routing section: dimmed progress text shown in place of the relay controls while SQLLY asks the account service which relay devices are registered.

relay_not_paired_hint.value: Ainda não autorizado — emparelhe este dispositivo para rotear por ele.
relay_not_paired_hint.location: Connection editor → Routing section → Relay device picker: dimmed hint under the device dropdown, left of the Authorize button, shown when the selected relay device is not paired with this computer yet.

relay_pairing_desktop_required.value: Não autorizado (o emparelhamento requer o aplicativo de desktop).
relay_pairing_desktop_required.location: Connection editor → Routing section → Relay device picker (browser version only): dimmed hint under the dropdown shown when the selected relay device is not paired, since pairing can only be done in the desktop app.

relay_revoke_button.location: Connection editor → Routing section → Relay device picker: button beside “Authorized for this account.”; opens an inline confirmation to remove the pairing with the selected relay device.

relay_revoke_cancel.location: Connection editor → Routing section → Revoke pairing confirmation: button that dismisses the inline confirmation and keeps the relay device paired.

relay_revoke_confirm.location: Connection editor → Routing section → Revoke pairing confirmation: red destructive button that removes the pairing between this computer and the selected relay device (verb).

relay_revoke_confirmation.value: Revogar o emparelhamento com “{device_name}”? As conexões roteadas através dele deixarão de funcionar até que seja autorizado novamente.
relay_revoke_confirmation.location: Connection editor → Routing → Relay: message “Revoke the pairing with “{device_name}”? Connections routed through it will stop working until it is…”

relay_revoke_failed.location: Connection editor → Routing section: relay error message shown when removing the pairing with a relay device fails; {error} is the server or network error detail.

relay_shared_device.location: Connection editor → Routing section → Relay device dropdown: entry for a relay device another account owner shared with you; {device_name} is that device's name, followed by a “shared” marker.

relay_signin_required_hint.value: Conecta diretamente. Faça login e registre um dispositivo de retransmissão para rotear esta conexão por ele.
relay_signin_required_hint.location: Connection editor → Routing section: dimmed help text shown in place of the relay controls when you are not signed in to a SQLLY account; the connection goes straight to the server.

relay_signin_to_authorize.value: Faça login para autorizar um dispositivo de retransmissão.
relay_signin_to_authorize.location: Connection editor → Routing section: relay error shown when Authorize is clicked but your SQLLY account session has expired or you are signed out.

relay_signin_to_revoke.value: Faça login para revogar um emparelhamento de retransmissão.
relay_signin_to_revoke.location: Connection editor → Routing section: relay error shown when a pairing revocation is confirmed but your SQLLY account session has expired or you are signed out.

rollback_label.location: Connection editor → Safety options: checkbox label; when on, every query on this connection runs inside a transaction that is rolled back afterwards, so no change is kept.

route_via_relay_label.value: Rotear por um dispositivo de retransmissão
route_via_relay_label.location: Connection editor → Routing section: checkbox label that sends this connection through one of your registered relay devices instead of connecting directly; reveals the relay device dropdown.

routing_section.location: Connection editor dialog → Routing section heading: heading shown below Environment for choosing whether the connection goes directly to the server or through a relay device.

save_button.location: Connection editor → Dialog footer: primary button at the far right that validates the form and saves the connection (disabled while the server name is invalid).

select_ca_certificate_title.value: Selecione um arquivo de certificado CA
select_ca_certificate_title.location: Connection editor → TLS options → CA file Browse button: title of the system open-file dialog for choosing the certificate authority (CA) file used to verify the server.

select_client_certificate_title.value: Selecione um arquivo de certificado de cliente
select_client_certificate_title.location: Connection editor → TLS options → Client certificate Browse button: title of the system open-file dialog for choosing the client certificate presented to the server.

select_client_key_title.value: Selecione um arquivo de chave do cliente
select_client_key_title.location: Connection editor → TLS options → Client key Browse button: title of the system open-file dialog for choosing the private key that goes with the client certificate.

select_private_key_title.value: Selecione um arquivo de chave privada
select_private_key_title.location: Connection editor → Tunnel / Proxy section → SSH tunnel → Private key file Browse button: title of the system open-file dialog for choosing the SSH private key.

sentinel_behavior_note.value: O host e a porta acima não são usados para conectar: toda conexão pergunta aos sentinelas qual é o mestre, faz login nele com o usuário e a senha abaixo e, após um failover, executa novamente apenas scripts somente leitura. Túneis SSH, proxies e rotas de retransmissão não estão disponíveis com o Sentinel.
sentinel_behavior_note.location: Connection editor → Redis options → Sentinel: dimmed explanation at the end of the Sentinel fields, shown when “Connect through Sentinel” is checked, describing how the master is found and failover handled.

sentinel_enable_label.value: Conectar através do Sentinel (pergunta aos sentinelas qual é o mestre atual)
sentinel_enable_label.location: Connection editor → Redis options: checkbox label that makes SQLLY ask Redis Sentinel servers for the current master instead of dialing Server/Port directly; reveals the Sentinel fields.

sentinel_host_required.value: Uma conexão do Sentinel precisa de pelo menos um host sentinela
sentinel_host_required.location: Connection editor → Redis → Sentinel: validation message shown when no Sentinel host is configured.

sentinel_hosts_label.value: Sentinelas (host:porta, separados por vírgula; porta 26379 quando omitida)
sentinel_hosts_label.location: Connection editor → Redis options → Sentinel: label above the input listing the sentinel servers as host:port, comma-separated (port 26379 if omitted); keep “host:port” and 26379.

sentinel_master_name_label.location: Connection editor → Redis options → Sentinel: label above the input for the name of the monitored master group the sentinels know (e.g. “mymaster”).

sentinel_master_required.value: O nome do mestre do Sentinel é obrigatório
sentinel_master_required.location: Connection editor → Validation errors: red error line at the bottom of the form shown when Save or Test Connection is clicked, when “Connect through Sentinel” is checked but the Sentinel Master name field is empty.

sentinel_password_label.location: Connection editor → Redis options → Sentinel: label above the masked input for the password used to sign in to the sentinel servers themselves (not the Redis data password).

sentinel_password_placeholder.location: Connection editor → Redis options → Sentinel → Sentinel password field: placeholder saying this password is only needed if the sentinels require authentication.

sentinel_prefer_replica_label.value: Preferir réplica para leituras (scripts somente leitura rodam em uma réplica íntegra)
sentinel_prefer_replica_label.location: Connection editor → Redis options → Sentinel: checkbox label; when on, read-only scripts run on a healthy replica instead of the master.

server_info_case_insensitive.location: Connection editor → Footer → Server info: value of the Identifiers row after a successful Test Connection, meaning the server treats table and column names as case-insensitive; short lowercase adjective.

server_info_case_sensitive.location: Connection editor → Footer → Server info: value of the Identifiers row after a successful Test Connection, meaning the server treats table and column names as case-sensitive; short lowercase adjective.

server_info_charset.location: Connection editor → Footer → Server info: row label, followed by a colon and the server default character set (e.g. utf8mb4), listed left of the buttons after a successful Test Connection.

server_info_collation.location: Connection editor → Footer → Server info: row label, followed by a colon and the server default collation name, listed after a successful Test Connection.

server_info_database.location: Connection editor → Footer → Server info: row label, followed by a colon and the name of the database the test session landed in, listed after a successful Test Connection.

server_info_encrypted.location: Connection editor → Footer → Server info: value of the TLS row after a successful Test Connection, meaning the test session used an encrypted (TLS) link; short lowercase adjective.

server_info_identifiers.location: Connection editor → Footer → Server info: row label, followed by a colon and “case-sensitive” or “case-insensitive”, describing how the server compares object names; shown after a successful Test Connection.

server_info_latency.location: Connection editor → Footer → Server info: row label, followed by a colon and the measured round-trip time to the server in milliseconds, listed after a successful Test Connection.

server_info_latency_value.location: Connection editor → Footer → Server info: value of the Latency row after a successful Test Connection; {milliseconds} is the measured round-trip time as a whole number, “ms” is the milliseconds unit abbreviation.

server_info_not_encrypted.location: Connection editor → Footer → Server info: value of the TLS row after a successful Test Connection, meaning the test session used an unencrypted link; short lowercase adjective.

server_info_product.location: Connection editor → Footer → Server info: first row label, followed by a colon and the database product name the server reported (e.g. PostgreSQL), listed after a successful Test Connection.

server_info_tls.location: Connection editor → Footer → Server info: row label, followed by a colon and “encrypted” or “not encrypted”, telling whether the test session used TLS; keep the acronym TLS.

server_info_user.location: Connection editor → Footer → Server info: row label, followed by a colon and the user name the server says the test session is signed in as, listed after a successful Test Connection.

server_info_version.location: Connection editor → Footer → Server info: row label, followed by a colon and the server version string, listed after a successful Test Connection.

server_label.location: Connection editor → Connection details: label above the server host name, named instance or IP address input, left of Port; replaced by “Database file” for file-based engines.

server_required.location: Connection editor → Validation errors: red error line at the bottom of the form shown when Save or Test Connection is clicked, when the Server field is empty for an engine that connects to a server.

signed_in_entra_users.location: Connection editor → Authentication section → Microsoft Entra: heading above the list of signed-in Entra accounts to pick from; {count} is the number of accounts listed.

sql_account_password_missing.value: A conta SQL salva “{account_name}” não possui senha no chaveiro do sistema.
sql_account_password_missing.location: Connection editor → Authentication: error message “The saved SQL account “{account_name}” has no password in the system keyring.”

sql_account_password_read_failed.value: Não foi possível ler a senha da conta SQL: {error}
sql_account_password_read_failed.location: Connection editor → Authentication section: red error at the bottom of the form shown when a saved SQL account is picked but its password cannot be read from the system keychain; {error} is the keychain error.

sql_accounts_empty.value: Nenhuma conta SQL salva. Insira as credenciais abaixo ou adicione uma em Gerenciamento de conexão > Contas.
sql_accounts_empty.location: Connection editor → Authentication section: dimmed empty-state text shown in place of the saved SQL account chips (SQL Login) when no accounts are saved; keep the menu path wording consistent with Connection Management.

sql_username_required.value: O nome de usuário é obrigatório para o login SQL
sql_username_required.location: Connection editor → Validation errors: red error line at the bottom of the form shown when Save or Test Connection is clicked, when the authentication method is SQL Login and the Username field is empty.

ssh_agent_option.location: Connection editor → Tunnel / Proxy section → SSH tunnel → Authentication dropdown: default option that signs in to the SSH server with keys held by the running SSH agent.

ssh_authentication_label.location: Connection editor → Tunnel / Proxy section → SSH tunnel: label above the dropdown choosing how to sign in to the SSH server (SSH agent / Private key file / Password), below SSH Username.

ssh_host_label.location: Connection editor → Tunnel / Proxy section → SSH tunnel: label above the SSH server (bastion) host name input, shown after “Connect through an SSH tunnel” is checked; short space.

ssh_host_required.location: Connection editor → Tunnel / Proxy section (also Tunnel Profiles dialog) → Validation errors: red error line shown when Save or Test Connection is clicked, when the SSH tunnel is enabled but its Host field is empty.

ssh_jump_host_required.value: O host intermediário SSH é obrigatório
ssh_jump_host_required.location: Connection editor → Tunnel / Proxy section (also Tunnel Profiles dialog) → Validation errors: red error line shown when Save or Test Connection is clicked, when “Use a jump host” is checked but the Jump host field is empty.

ssh_jump_port_invalid.value: A porta do host intermediário SSH deve ser 1–65535
ssh_jump_port_invalid.location: Connection editor → Tunnel / Proxy section (also Tunnel Profiles dialog) → Validation errors: red error line shown when Save or Test Connection is clicked, when “Use a jump host” is checked and the jump host Port is not a number from 1 to 65535.

ssh_jump_username_required.value: O nome de usuário do host intermediário SSH é obrigatório
ssh_jump_username_required.location: Connection editor → Tunnel / Proxy section (also Tunnel Profiles dialog) → Validation errors: red error line shown when Save or Test Connection is clicked, when “Use a jump host” is checked but the Jump username field is empty.

ssh_keepalive_invalid.value: O keepalive SSH deve ser um número de segundos (0 desativa)
ssh_keepalive_invalid.location: Connection editor → Tunnel / Proxy section (also Tunnel Profiles dialog) → Validation errors: red error line shown when Save or Test Connection is clicked, when Keepalive (seconds) is not a whole number of seconds up to 86400; 0 disables keepalive messages.

ssh_passphrase_label.location: Connection editor → Tunnel / Proxy section → SSH tunnel: label above the masked input for the passphrase that unlocks the private key file, shown when Authentication is “Private key file”.

ssh_password_label.location: Connection editor → Tunnel / Proxy section → SSH tunnel: label above the masked SSH password input, shown when Authentication is “Password”.

ssh_password_required.location: Connection editor → Tunnel / Proxy section (also Tunnel Profiles dialog) → Validation errors: red error line shown when Save or Test Connection is clicked, when SSH Authentication is “Password” and no password is entered or saved.

ssh_port_invalid.location: Connection editor → Tunnel / Proxy section (also Tunnel Profiles dialog) → Validation errors: red error line shown when Save or Test Connection is clicked, when the SSH tunnel Port (next to SSH Host) is not a number from 1 to 65535.

ssh_port_label.location: Connection editor → Tunnel / Proxy section → SSH tunnel: label above the narrow SSH server port input (default 22) to the right of the SSH Host field; short space.

ssh_private_key_required.value: O arquivo de chave privada é obrigatório
ssh_private_key_required.location: Connection editor → Tunnel / Proxy section (also Tunnel Profiles dialog) → Validation errors: red error line shown when Save or Test Connection is clicked, when SSH Authentication is “Private key file” and the Private key file path is empty.

ssh_secret_placeholder.location: Connection editor → Tunnel / Proxy section → SSH tunnel: masked placeholder in the secret input, which is labeled Password or Passphrase depending on the chosen SSH authentication.

ssh_secret_required.location: Connection editor → Tunnel / Proxy section (also Tunnel Profiles dialog) → Validation errors: red error line shown when Save or Test Connection is clicked, when the SSH tunnel needs a secret (password or passphrase) and none is entered or saved.

ssh_tunnel_browser_unavailable.value: Os túneis SSH não estão disponíveis quando o SQLLY é executado em um navegador
ssh_tunnel_browser_unavailable.location: Connection editor → Tunnel / Proxy section: dimmed text shown instead of the tunnel fields when SQLLY runs in a browser served by your organization’s server, where SSH tunnels cannot be opened.

ssh_tunnel_desktop_required.value: Os túneis SSH precisam do aplicativo de desktop
ssh_tunnel_desktop_required.location: Connection editor → Tunnel / Proxy section: dimmed text shown instead of the tunnel fields in the browser preview (demo) of SQLLY, pointing out that SSH tunnels need the desktop app.

ssh_tunnel_duckdb_unavailable.value: O DuckDB abre um arquivo local; não há servidor para onde criar um túnel
ssh_tunnel_duckdb_unavailable.location: Connection editor → Tunnel / Proxy section: dimmed text shown instead of the tunnel fields when the engine is DuckDB, which opens a local file, so there is nothing to tunnel to.

ssh_tunnel_engine_unavailable.value: Os túneis SSH ainda não estão disponíveis para este mecanismo
ssh_tunnel_engine_unavailable.location: Connection editor → Tunnel / Proxy section: dimmed text shown instead of the tunnel fields when the selected database engine does not support SSH tunnels yet.

ssh_tunnel_sqlite_unavailable.value: O SQLite abre um arquivo local; não há servidor para onde criar um túnel
ssh_tunnel_sqlite_unavailable.location: Connection editor → Tunnel / Proxy section: dimmed text shown instead of the tunnel fields when the engine is SQLite, which opens a local file, so there is nothing to tunnel to.

ssh_username_label.location: Connection editor dialog → Tunnel / Proxy section → SSH tunnel fields: label above the input for the user name to log in to the SSH server with; shown after “Connect through an SSH tunnel” is checked, below the SSH host and port.

ssh_username_required.value: O nome de usuário SSH é obrigatório
ssh_username_required.location: Connection editor dialog → Form error line: inline validation error shown below the form on Save or Test when the SSH tunnel is enabled but its username field is empty.

startup_sql_label.location: Connection editor dialog → Connection options: label above the multi-line box for SQL statements that run automatically each time this connection opens; sits right below the Timeout field.

startup_sql_placeholder.value: SQL opcional executado ao abrir a conexão
startup_sql_placeholder.location: Connection editor dialog → Connection options: grey placeholder inside the empty Startup SQL box, explaining that the field is optional SQL executed whenever the connection is opened.

notes_placeholder.value: Observações opcionais: quem é o responsável por este servidor, para que ele serve e o que merece atenção
notes_placeholder.location: Connection editor dialog → Notes box: grey placeholder inside the empty Notes box suggesting what to write there (owner, purpose, cautions).

notes_label.location: Connection editor dialog → Notes: label above the multi-line Notes box at the bottom of the form, below Client and Project, where the user keeps free-form notes about this connection.

test_button.location: Connection editor dialog → Footer: button at the bottom left that tries to connect with the current form values without saving; a verb meaning “test the connection”, keep it very short.

test_connected.location: Connection editor dialog → Footer status: green success message beside the Test button after a connection test succeeds; {latency_ms} is how many milliseconds the connection took.

test_connected_with_report.location: Connection editor dialog → Footer status: green success message after a Redis Sentinel connection test succeeds; {latency_ms} is the connect time in milliseconds and {report} names which master answered and which sentinel reported it.

test_failed.location: Connection editor dialog → Footer status: red summary beside the Test button when a connection test fails; the detailed reason is shown separately in the form’s error line.

test_running_button.location: Connection editor dialog → Footer: label that temporarily replaces the Test button while a connection test is in progress; short progressive verb form.

timeout_label.location: Connection editor dialog → Connection options: label above the numeric input for how many seconds to wait for the server before a connection attempt gives up.

title_duplicate.location: Connection editor dialog → Title bar (duplicate mode): text shown when the editor is opened by duplicating an existing connection, so the user is creating a new copy of it.

title_edit.location: Connection editor dialog → Title bar (edit mode): text shown when the editor is opened to change an existing saved connection.

title_new.location: Connection editor dialog → Title bar (new mode): text shown when the editor is opened to create a brand-new connection from scratch.

title_view.location: Connection editor dialog → Title bar (view-only mode): text shown for a read-only connection provided by a relay proxy, which can be inspected and tested but not saved.

tls_browse_button.location: Connection editor dialog → TLS section: button to the right of the CA file, client certificate and client key path inputs that opens a file picker to choose that file (desktop app only).

tls_client_pair_required.value: O certificado do cliente e a chave do cliente devem ser definidos
tls_client_pair_required.location: Connection editor dialog → Form error line: inline validation error on Save or Test when only one of the TLS client certificate and client key paths is filled in; both are needed together.

tls_disable.location: Connection editor dialog → TLS section → TLS dropdown: option that turns off encryption so the connection is made without TLS.

tls_label.location: Connection editor dialog → TLS section: label above the dropdown choosing the TLS mode (disable, require without verification, verify CA, verify full) for PostgreSQL, MySQL, ClickHouse, libSQL and Redis connections.

tls_require_unverified.location: Connection editor dialog → TLS section → TLS dropdown: option that encrypts the connection but does not verify the server certificate; the wording must make clear it is not a verified mode.

tls_verify_ca.location: Connection editor dialog → TLS section → TLS dropdown: option that encrypts and checks that the server certificate is signed by a trusted certificate authority, without checking the host name.

tls_verify_full.location: Connection editor dialog → TLS section → TLS dropdown: strictest option, which encrypts and verifies both the certificate authority and that the certificate matches the server host name.

transport_kube_combination_invalid.value: O encaminhamento de porta do Kubernetes não pode ser combinado com SSH ou saltos de proxy
transport_kube_combination_invalid.location: Connection editor dialog → Form error line: inline validation error on Save or Test when kubectl port-forward is enabled together with an SSH tunnel or proxy hop, which is not allowed.

transport_too_many_hops.value: A cadeia de transporte não pode exceder dois saltos
transport_too_many_hops.location: Connection editor dialog → Form error line: inline validation error on Save or Test when the proxy, SSH tunnel and jump host settings add up to more than two network hops before the database.

trust_certificate_label.location: Connection editor dialog → Connection options: checkbox under “Encrypt connection” for engines without a TLS dropdown (such as SQL Server) that accepts the server’s certificate without validating it.

trust_os_roots_label.value: Confiar também nas raízes do chaveiro do SO
trust_os_roots_label.location: Connection editor dialog → TLS section: checkbox shown for Redis when the TLS mode is Verify CA or Verify full; also accepts certificates signed by authorities installed in the operating system’s trust store.

tunnel_profile_label.location: Connection editor dialog → Tunnel / Proxy section: label above the dropdown choosing a saved, reusable tunnel profile, or “None (inline)” to enter proxy and SSH settings directly in this form.

tunnel_profile_missing.value: O perfil do túnel não existe mais
tunnel_profile_missing.location: Connection editor dialog → Tunnel / Proxy section: grey summary line under the Tunnel profile dropdown shown when the connection points to a tunnel profile that has since been deleted.

tunnel_proxy_section.location: Connection editor dialog → Tunnel / Proxy section heading: heading over the tunnel profile picker, proxy first hop and SSH tunnel settings used to reach the database through intermediate hosts.

unsupported_engine.value: {engine_name} não é compatível com esta build
unsupported_engine.location: Connection editor dialog → Form error line: error shown after pasting a connection URL or opening a connection link whose database engine cannot be used in this edition; {engine_name} is the engine’s display name.

use_jump_host_label.location: Connection editor dialog → Tunnel / Proxy section → SSH tunnel fields: checkbox below the keep-alive field that reveals extra fields for an intermediate SSH jump (bastion) host the tunnel passes through first.

use_kube_port_forward_label.location: Connection editor dialog → Kubernetes port-forward section: checkbox that enables reaching the database through a kubectl port-forward to a pod or service, revealing the context, namespace and target fields.

use_no_account.location: Connection editor dialog → Authentication section → Microsoft Entra account list: clickable row at the end of the signed-in accounts list that clears the account choice so no Entra account is attached to this connection.

use_proxy_label.value: Usar um proxy como primeiro salto
use_proxy_label.location: Connection editor dialog → Tunnel / Proxy section: checkbox that routes the connection through a SOCKS5 or HTTP proxy as the first hop, revealing the proxy kind, host, port, username and password fields.

use_ssh_tunnel_label.location: Connection editor dialog → Tunnel / Proxy section: checkbox that routes the connection through an SSH server, revealing the SSH host, port, username, authentication and jump host fields.

username_label.location: Connection editor dialog → Authentication section: label above the database login name input, shown when the SQL login (username and password) authentication mode is selected.

add_button.location: Manage Clients, Projects & Environments dialog → Left list: button under the list of clients, projects or environments that creates a new entry of the active tab’s kind and selects it for renaming.

added_client.location: Manage Clients, Projects & Environments dialog → Status line: confirmation at the bottom left after “+ Add” creates a new client on the Clients tab.

added_environment.location: Manage Clients, Projects & Environments dialog → Status line: confirmation at the bottom left after “+ Add” creates a new environment on the Environments tab.

added_project.location: Manage Clients, Projects & Environments dialog → Status line: confirmation at the bottom left after “+ Add” creates a new project on the Projects tab.

browse_icon_button.location: Manage Clients, Projects & Environments dialog → Detail form → Icon: button to the right of the icon path input that opens a file picker for choosing an image to use as the entry’s icon.

browser_icon_picker_unavailable.value: Não é possível escolher um arquivo de ícone
browser_icon_picker_unavailable.location: Manage Clients, Projects & Environments dialog → Status line: message in the browser version when Browse… is clicked next to the icon path, because picking a local image file is not possible there.

client_singular.location: Connection Management → Clients pane → Editor: heading of the first group, holding the Name field, when a client is selected; singular noun.

clients_tab.location: Manage Clients, Projects & Environments dialog → Tabs: first tab along the top, listing the clients that connections can be assigned to.

close_picker_button.location: Manage Clients, Projects & Environments dialog → Detail form → Color: label of the toggle button beside the color input while the inline color picker is open; clicking it hides the picker.

color_invalid.location: Manage Clients, Projects & Environments dialog → Detail form → Color: red hint under the color input when the typed text is not a valid hex color such as #1A2B3C.

color_label.location: Manage Clients, Projects & Environments dialog → Detail form: label above the hex color input, swatch and picker button that set the color used to tag this client, project or environment.

color_optional.location: Manage Clients, Projects & Environments dialog → Detail form → Color: grey hint under the color input when it is empty, saying a color does not have to be set.

color_valid.location: Manage Clients, Projects & Environments dialog → Detail form → Color: grey hint under the color input confirming the typed text is a valid hex color.

dialog_title.location: Manage Clients, Projects & Environments dialog → Title bar: title bar of the dialog opened from Tools → Manage entities for editing clients, projects and environments and their query protections.

empty_clients.location: Manage Clients, Projects & Environments dialog → Left list: placeholder text in the empty list on the Clients tab before any client exists.

empty_environments.location: Manage Clients, Projects & Environments dialog → Left list: placeholder text in the empty list on the Environments tab before any environment exists.

empty_projects.location: Manage Clients, Projects & Environments dialog → Left list: placeholder text in the empty list on the Projects tab before any project exists.

environment_singular.location: Connection Management → Environments pane → Editor: heading of the first group, holding the Name field, when an environment is selected; singular noun.

environments_tab.location: Manage Clients, Projects & Environments dialog → Tabs: third tab along the top, listing environments (such as development or production) that connections can be tagged with.

icon_label.location: Manage Clients, Projects & Environments dialog → Detail form: label above the icon path input and Browse… button that set an optional image shown for this client, project or environment.

icon_path_placeholder.location: Manage Clients, Projects & Environments dialog → Detail form → Icon: grey placeholder inside the empty icon path input, inviting an optional path to an image file.

image_file_filter.location: Manage Clients, Projects & Environments dialog → Detail form → Icon → Browse… file picker: name of the file-type filter that limits the picker to image files (PNG, JPEG, GIF, SVG, ICO, BMP, WebP).

name_label.location: Manage Clients, Projects & Environments dialog → Detail form: label above the name input at the top of the form for the selected client, project or environment.

name_placeholder.location: Manage Clients, Projects & Environments dialog → Detail form → Name: grey placeholder inside the empty name input for the selected client, project or environment.

name_required.location: Manage Clients, Projects & Environments dialog → Status line: error at the bottom left when Save is clicked while the name input is empty.

new_client.location: Manage Clients, Projects & Environments dialog → Left list: default name given to a client created with “+ Add” on the Clients tab, until the user types a real name.

new_environment.location: Manage Clients, Projects & Environments dialog → Left list: default name given to an environment created with “+ Add” on the Environments tab, until the user types a real name.

new_project.location: Manage Clients, Projects & Environments dialog → Left list: default name given to a project created with “+ Add” on the Projects tab, until the user types a real name.

pick_color_button.location: Manage Clients, Projects & Environments dialog → Detail form → Color: button beside the color input and swatch that opens an inline color picker below it; changes to “Close Picker” while open.

project_singular.location: Connection Management → Projects pane → Editor: heading of the first group, holding the Name field, when a project is selected; singular noun.

projects_tab.location: Manage Clients, Projects & Environments dialog → Tabs: second tab along the top, listing the projects that connections can be grouped under.

query_protections_section.location: Manage Clients, Projects & Environments dialog → Detail form: section heading above the safety checkboxes (read-only, confirmations, Touch ID, rollback) applied to every connection in this client, project or environment.

remove_button.location: Manage Clients, Projects & Environments dialog → Left list: button beside “+ Add” that deletes the selected client, project or environment; disabled when nothing is selected.

removed.location: Manage Clients, Projects & Environments dialog → Status line: confirmation at the bottom left after Remove deletes the selected client, project or environment.

safety_ai_review_description.value: Exige uma revisão gerada por IA antes de executar instruções que alteram dados.
safety_ai_review_description.location: Manage Clients, Projects & Environments dialog → Detail form → Query Protections: grey explanation under the “Require AI review for data changes” checkbox; data-changing statements must get an AI-written review before they run.

safety_ai_review_label.value: Exigir revisão de IA para alterações de dados
safety_ai_review_label.location: Manage Clients, Projects & Environments dialog → Detail form → Query Protections: checkbox label (also a row label in Connection Management’s entity editor) that requires an AI review before INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE and similar statements run.

safety_confirmation_description.value: Solicita confirmação antes de executar instruções que alteram dados.
safety_confirmation_description.location: Manage Clients, Projects & Environments dialog → Detail form → Query Protections: grey explanation under the confirmation-dialog checkbox; the user is asked to confirm before any data-changing statement runs.

safety_confirmation_label.value: Exigir caixa de diálogo de confirmação antes de executar
safety_confirmation_label.location: Manage Clients, Projects & Environments dialog → Detail form → Query Protections: checkbox label (also a row label in Connection Management’s entity editor) that shows a confirmation dialog before data-changing statements are run.

safety_production_description.value: As conexões neste ambiente ficam somente leitura até que você libere gravações por um tempo limitado, e cada alteração de dados pede confirmação mostrando o SQL exato.
safety_production_description.location: Manage Clients, Projects & Environments dialog → Detail form → Query Protections: grey explanation under the “Production environment” checkbox; connections stay read-only until writes are unlocked for a limited time, and each change asks for confirmation with its SQL.

safety_production_label.location: Manage Clients, Projects & Environments dialog → Detail form → Query Protections: first checkbox label (also a row label in Connection Management’s entity editor) that marks the entry as production, turning on read-only mode and timed write unlocks.

safety_rollback_description.value: Envolve cada lote em uma transação revertida automaticamente.
safety_rollback_description.location: Manage Clients, Projects & Environments dialog → Detail form → Query Protections: grey explanation under the transaction + rollback checkbox; each executed batch runs inside a transaction that is always rolled back, so no changes persist.

safety_rollback_label.location: Manage Clients, Projects & Environments dialog → Detail form → Query Protections: checkbox label (also a row label in Connection Management’s entity editor) that wraps every execution in a transaction and rolls it back afterwards.

safety_select_only_description.value: Bloqueia INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE e outras instruções não-SELECT.
safety_select_only_description.location: Manage Clients, Projects & Environments dialog → Detail form → Query Protections: grey explanation under the “Block all but SELECT” checkbox; INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE and any other non-SELECT statement is refused.

safety_select_only_label.location: Manage Clients, Projects & Environments dialog → Detail form → Query Protections: checkbox label (also a row label in Connection Management’s entity editor) that only allows SELECT queries; SQL keywords stay untranslated.

safety_touch_connect_description.value: Exige Touch ID antes de conectar.
safety_touch_connect_description.location: Manage Clients, Projects & Environments dialog → Detail form → Query Protections: grey explanation under the “Require Touch ID to connect” checkbox; a Touch ID fingerprint check is needed before the connection opens.

safety_touch_connect_label.location: Manage Clients, Projects & Environments dialog → Detail form → Query Protections: checkbox label (also a row label in Connection Management’s entity editor) requiring a Touch ID fingerprint check before connecting; Touch ID is Apple’s product name.

safety_touch_non_select_description.value: Exige Touch ID antes de executar instruções não-SELECT.
safety_touch_non_select_description.location: Manage Clients, Projects & Environments dialog → Detail form → Query Protections: grey explanation under the “Require Touch ID for non-SELECT” checkbox; a Touch ID check is needed before running any statement other than SELECT.

safety_touch_non_select_label.location: Manage Clients, Projects & Environments dialog → Detail form → Query Protections: checkbox label (also a row label in Connection Management’s entity editor) requiring a Touch ID check before any non-SELECT statement runs.

safety_unbounded_delete_description.value: Permite DELETE sem cláusula WHERE nem confirmação extra.
safety_unbounded_delete_description.location: Manage Clients, Projects & Environments dialog → Detail form → Query Protections: grey explanation under the “Allow unconstrained DELETE” checkbox; a DELETE with no WHERE clause runs without the usual extra confirmation.

safety_unbounded_delete_label.location: Manage Clients, Projects & Environments dialog → Detail form → Query Protections: checkbox label (also a row label in Connection Management’s entity editor) that lets DELETE statements without a WHERE clause run without an extra warning.

safety_unbounded_update_description.value: Permite UPDATE sem cláusula WHERE nem confirmação extra.
safety_unbounded_update_description.location: Manage Clients, Projects & Environments dialog → Detail form → Query Protections: grey explanation under the “Allow unconstrained UPDATE” checkbox; an UPDATE with no WHERE clause runs without the usual extra confirmation.

safety_unbounded_update_label.location: Manage Clients, Projects & Environments dialog → Detail form → Query Protections: checkbox label (also a row label in Connection Management’s entity editor) that lets UPDATE statements without a WHERE clause run without an extra warning.

save_button.location: Manage Clients, Projects & Environments dialog → Footer: primary button at the bottom right that saves the name, color, icon and query protections of the selected entry.

saved_named.location: Manage Clients, Projects & Environments dialog → Status line: confirmation at the bottom left after Save succeeds; {entity_name} is the saved client, project or environment name.

select_icon_title.location: Manage Clients, Projects & Environments dialog → Detail form → Icon → Browse…: title of the native file picker window opened to choose an icon image.

untitled_row.location: Manage Clients, Projects & Environments dialog → Left list: fallback text shown for a client, project or environment whose name is blank.

account_registration_failed.value: Não foi possível registrar a conta Microsoft Entra: {error}
account_registration_failed.location: Microsoft Entra Users dialog → Status line: error detail, shown after “Sign-in failed:”, when sign-in succeeded but the account could not be added to SQLLY’s list of Entra accounts; {error} is the technical reason.

account_removed.location: Microsoft Entra Users dialog → Status line: green confirmation after the second click on Confirm removal deletes an account; {account_label} is the account’s display name or user name.

add_user.location: Microsoft Entra Users dialog → Footer: primary button that opens the web browser to sign in a new Microsoft Entra account; replaced by “Signing in…” while that is in progress.

browser_signin_unavailable.value: O login do Microsoft Entra não está disponível
browser_signin_unavailable.location: Microsoft Entra Users dialog → Status line: error detail in the browser version when Add User is clicked, because Microsoft Entra sign-in cannot run inside a web page.

confirm_removal.location: Microsoft Entra Users dialog → Footer: red label the Remove button switches to after its first click; clicking again permanently signs the selected account out, Escape cancels.

dialog_subtitle.value: Contas conectadas disponíveis para o gerenciador de conexões.
dialog_subtitle.location: Microsoft Entra Users dialog → Header: grey one-line description next to the Entra icon at the top of the dialog body, explaining the list shows signed-in accounts usable by connections.

dialog_title.location: Microsoft Entra Users dialog → Title bar: title bar of the dialog that lists, adds, refreshes and removes Microsoft Entra (Azure AD) accounts used for database sign-in.

empty_accounts.value: Nenhuma conta ainda – escolha Adicionar usuário para entrar no Microsoft Entra.
empty_accounts.location: Microsoft Entra Users dialog → Account list: centered empty-state text when no Entra accounts are signed in yet, pointing the user to the Add User button.

fallback_account_detail.location: Microsoft Entra Users dialog → Account list: grey second line of an account row when neither its user name nor its tenant ID is known.

keychain_failed.value: Não foi possível salvar os tokens do Microsoft Entra no chaveiro do sistema: {error}
keychain_failed.location: Microsoft Entra Users dialog → Status line: error detail, shown after “Sign-in failed:”, when the account’s sign-in tokens could not be stored in the operating system keychain; {error} is the technical reason.

oauth_failed.value: Falha no login do Microsoft Entra: {error}
oauth_failed.location: Microsoft Entra Users dialog → Status line: error detail, shown after “Sign-in failed:”, when the browser-based Microsoft sign-in itself fails or is cancelled; {error} is the reason returned.

preview_browser_banner.value: Apenas ilustrativo: a visualização da Web não pode entrar no Microsoft Entra nem acessar o Azure. Use o aplicativo de desktop para adicionar contas reais.
preview_browser_banner.location: Microsoft Entra Users dialog → Banner: notice at the top of the dialog in the public web demo, saying the accounts shown are examples and real accounts must be added in the desktop app.

refresh_account.location: Microsoft Entra Users dialog → Account list: small button at the right of each account row that re-runs browser sign-in to renew that account’s expired credentials.

refreshing_account.location: Microsoft Entra Users dialog → Account list: label that replaces the Refresh button on the one row whose credentials are being renewed.

remove_account.location: Microsoft Entra Users dialog → Footer: button beside Add User that starts removing the selected account; the first click asks for confirmation.

remove_confirmation.value: Remover {account_label}? Isso desconecta a conta do SQLLY neste computador. Sua conta da Microsoft não será afetada.
remove_confirmation.location: Microsoft Entra Users dialog → Status line: confirmation prompt after the first click on Remove, explaining what removal does; {account_label} is the account’s display name or user name.

served_browser_banner.value: SQLLY no navegador não consegue entrar no Microsoft Entra. As conexões que precisam de uma conta Entra são configuradas pelo seu administrador.
served_browser_banner.location: Microsoft Entra Users dialog → Banner: notice at the top of the dialog when SQLLY runs in a browser served by an organization, saying Entra sign-in is unavailable and an administrator sets up such connections.

signin_coordination_failed.value: Não foi possível concluir o fluxo de login do Microsoft Entra: {error}
signin_coordination_failed.location: Microsoft Entra Users dialog → Status line: error detail, shown after “Sign-in failed:”, when the background sign-in task stops unexpectedly before finishing; {error} is the technical reason.

signin_failed.location: Microsoft Entra Users dialog → Status line: red error after adding or refreshing an account fails, shown with a Try again button; {error} is the specific failure reason.

signin_succeeded.value: Login realizado como {account_label}. Tokens salvos no chaveiro do sistema.
signin_succeeded.location: Microsoft Entra Users dialog → Status line: green confirmation after browser sign-in finishes and the account is added or refreshed; {account_label} is the account’s display name or user name.

signing_in.location: Microsoft Entra Users dialog → Footer: disabled label that replaces the Add User button while a browser sign-in is in progress.

tenant_only_detail.location: Microsoft Entra Users dialog → Account list: grey second line of an account row when only the tenant is known; {tenant_id} is the Microsoft Entra directory (tenant) ID.

tokens_in_keychain.value: Os tokens ficam no chaveiro do sistema.
tokens_in_keychain.location: Microsoft Entra Users dialog → Status line: default grey note when the dialog opens or an action is cancelled, reassuring that sign-in tokens are kept in the operating system keychain.

try_again.location: Microsoft Entra Users dialog → Status line: button to the right of a sign-in error that repeats the failed add or refresh attempt.

untitled_user.location: Microsoft Entra Users dialog → Account list and status line: fallback name for an account that has neither a display name nor a user name.

username_tenant_detail.location: Microsoft Entra Users dialog → Account list: grey second line of an account row; {username} is the sign-in name and {tenant_id} the Microsoft Entra directory (tenant) ID, separated by a bullet.

waiting_for_refresh.value: Aguardando você concluir o login no navegador para atualizar {account_label}.
waiting_for_refresh.location: Microsoft Entra Users dialog → Status line: progress message after clicking Refresh on a row while the browser sign-in to renew that account is open; {account_label} is the account’s name.

waiting_for_signin.value: Aguardando você concluir o login no Microsoft Entra pelo navegador.
waiting_for_signin.location: Microsoft Entra Users dialog → Status line: progress message after clicking Add User while the user completes the Microsoft Entra sign-in in their web browser.

add_button.location: Server Firewall Is Blocking Your IP dialog → Footer: primary button, enabled while the rule form is editable, that sends the rule name and address range to Azure to create or update the server firewall rule.

address_help.value: Deixe os dois endereços iguais para permitir apenas este IP. A reutilização de um nome de regra atualiza essa regra em vez de adicionar outra.
address_help.location: Server Firewall Is Blocking Your IP dialog → Rule form: small dimmed help line under the Start IP and End IP fields explaining that equal addresses allow a single IP and that an existing rule name is overwritten.

applied_body.location: Server Firewall Is Blocking Your IP dialog → Result: success message replacing the form after Azure accepts the rule; {server} is the server host name, {range} the single IP or start–end range, {rule_name} the rule; warns that reconnecting may fail for a few minutes.

cancel_button.location: Server Firewall Is Blocking Your IP dialog → Footer: secondary button beside Add Firewall Rule that dismisses the prompt without contacting Azure; disabled while the request is in flight.

close_button.location: Server Firewall Is Blocking Your IP dialog → Footer: only button left once the dialog shows a final result or explains it cannot add the rule; closes the dialog.

contacting_azure.value: Entrando em contato com o Azure…
contacting_azure.location: Server Firewall Is Blocking Your IP dialog → Status line: dimmed progress text under the form while the firewall rule request is being sent to Azure and the form is locked.

dialog_title.value: O firewall do servidor está bloqueando seu IP
dialog_title.location: Server Firewall Is Blocking Your IP dialog → Title bar: dialog title, shown when an Azure SQL server refuses the connection (error 40615) because the client IP is not on its firewall allow-list.

end_ip_label.location: Server Firewall Is Blocking Your IP dialog → Rule form: short label left of the input for the last IPv4 address of the range to allow (prefilled with the blocked IP; label column is narrow).

flow_account_not_registered.value: A conta Microsoft Entra no perfil ativo não está registrada. Faça login via Conexão do Azure SQL… e tente novamente.
flow_account_not_registered.location: Server Firewall Is Blocking Your IP dialog and Application menu bar → Tools menu → Add My IP to Firewall result window: explanation shown instead of the form when the connection’s Microsoft Entra account was never signed in on this machine; points to the Azure SQL Connection… menu item to sign in.

flow_applied.location: Application menu bar → Tools menu → Add My IP to Firewall result window: success message after the Tools-menu command looked up your public IP and added a rule; {server_fqdn} is the server, {range} the IP or range, {rule_name} the generated rule name.

flow_failed.value:
Não foi possível adicionar a regra de firewall.

{error}
flow_failed.location: Server Firewall Is Blocking Your IP dialog → Result and Application menu bar → Tools menu → Add My IP to Firewall result window: generic failure message when Azure or the token refresh returns an unclassified error; {error} is the underlying error detail shown on the following lines.

flow_forbidden.value:
Parece que você não tem permissão para alterar o firewall de {server_fqdn}.

O Azure recusou a alteração porque a conta com que você fez login não tem a permissão Microsoft.Sql/servers/firewallRules/write neste servidor. Você vai precisar pedir a alguém que a tenha — um administrador do Azure ou qualquer pessoa com a função Colaborador do SQL Server no servidor — para adicionar a regra para você (ou para lhe conceder essa permissão).
flow_forbidden.location: Server Firewall Is Blocking Your IP dialog → Result and Application menu bar → Tools menu → Add My IP to Firewall result window: error when Azure answers 403 because the signed-in account lacks permission to write firewall rules on {server_fqdn}; tells the user to ask an Azure administrator.

flow_ip_lookup_failed.location: Application menu bar → Tools menu → Add My IP to Firewall result window: error when the Tools-menu command cannot learn your public IPv4 from the api.ipify.org echo service; {error} is the network error detail; suggests adding the IP in the Azure portal.

flow_no_entra_binding.value: A conta Microsoft Entra no perfil ativo não está na lista de contas registradas. Faça login via Conexão do Azure SQL… e tente novamente.
flow_no_entra_binding.location: Application menu bar → Tools menu → Add My IP to Firewall result window: error shown when the active connection has no Microsoft Entra account attached (for example it uses SQL authentication), so there is no Azure credential to change the firewall with.

flow_no_subscriptions.value: Nenhuma assinatura do Azure está acessível à conta conectada. Faça login com uma conta que tenha acesso à assinatura do servidor.
flow_no_subscriptions.location: Server Firewall Is Blocking Your IP dialog → Result and Application menu bar → Tools menu → Add My IP to Firewall result window: error when the signed-in Azure account can see no subscriptions at all, so the server cannot be located to add the rule.

flow_not_azure_profile.value: O perfil ativo não é um servidor do Azure SQL. Conecte-se a um servidor *.database.windows.net (ou *.database.azure.com) e tente novamente.
flow_not_azure_profile.location: Application menu bar → Tools menu → Add My IP to Firewall result window: error for when the active connection is not an Azure SQL server host (*.database.windows.net or *.database.azure.com); asks the user to connect to one first.

flow_server_not_found.value: Não foi possível encontrar {server_fqdn} em nenhuma assinatura do Azure acessível à sua conta conectada. Confirme que você está conectado ao locatário correto e tem pelo menos acesso de leitor à assinatura do servidor.
flow_server_not_found.location: Server Firewall Is Blocking Your IP dialog → Result and Application menu bar → Tools menu → Add My IP to Firewall result window: error when {server_fqdn} (the server host name) is not found in any Azure subscription the signed-in account can read; suggests checking tenant and Reader access.

flow_signin_required.value: O login no Microsoft Entra é necessário ou expirou. Use Conexão do Azure SQL… para entrar e tente novamente.
flow_signin_required.location: Server Firewall Is Blocking Your IP dialog → Result and Application menu bar → Tools menu → Add My IP to Firewall result window: error when the cached Microsoft Entra sign-in is missing or expired and cannot be refreshed silently; tells the user to sign in again via Azure SQL Connection….

prompt_with_account.value: O servidor do Azure SQL {server} recusou a conexão porque o IP do seu cliente não está na lista de permissões do firewall (erro 40615). O SQLLY pode adicionar uma regra de firewall para esse endereço usando sua conta do Azure conectada ({account}), que precisa de permissão para alterar o firewall deste servidor. Nada é enviado ao Azure até você escolher Adicionar regra de firewall.
prompt_with_account.location: Server Firewall Is Blocking Your IP dialog → Intro paragraph: variant used when the server’s error did not name the blocked client IP but the signing-in Azure account is known; {server} is the server, {account} the account name.

prompt_with_ip.value: O servidor do Azure SQL {server} recusou a conexão porque o IP do seu cliente ({client_ip}) não está na lista de permissões do firewall (erro 40615). O SQLLY pode adicionar uma regra de firewall para esse endereço usando sua conta do Azure conectada. Nada é enviado ao Azure até você escolher Adicionar regra de firewall.
prompt_with_ip.location: Server Firewall Is Blocking Your IP dialog → Intro paragraph: variant used when the server named the blocked IP but the Azure account name is unknown; {server} is the server, {client_ip} the refused address.

prompt_with_ip_and_account.value: O servidor do Azure SQL {server} recusou a conexão porque o IP do seu cliente ({client_ip}) não está na lista de permissões do firewall (erro 40615). O SQLLY pode adicionar uma regra de firewall para esse endereço usando sua conta do Azure conectada ({account}), que precisa de permissão para alterar o firewall deste servidor. Nada é enviado ao Azure até você escolher Adicionar regra de firewall.
prompt_with_ip_and_account.location: Server Firewall Is Blocking Your IP dialog → Intro paragraph: variant used when both the blocked client IP and the Azure account are known; {server} is the server, {client_ip} the refused address, {account} the account name.

prompt_without_ip_or_account.value: O servidor do Azure SQL {server} recusou a conexão porque o IP do seu cliente não está na lista de permissões do firewall (erro 40615). O SQLLY pode adicionar uma regra de firewall para esse endereço usando sua conta do Azure conectada. Nada é enviado ao Azure até você escolher Adicionar regra de firewall.
prompt_without_ip_or_account.location: Server Firewall Is Blocking Your IP dialog → Intro paragraph: variant used when neither the blocked client IP nor the Azure account name is known; {server} is the Azure SQL server host name.

public_ip_network_error.value: Erro de rede ao entrar em contato com {endpoint}: {error}
public_ip_network_error.location: Application menu bar → Tools menu → Add My IP to Firewall result window: error detail inserted into the “could not determine your public IP” message when the request to the IP echo service fails; {endpoint} is the service URL, {error} the network error.

rule_name_label.location: Server Firewall Is Blocking Your IP dialog → Rule form: short label left of the first input, holding the Azure firewall rule name (prefilled like SQLLY-user-date); label column is narrow.

start_ip_label.location: Server Firewall Is Blocking Your IP dialog → Rule form: short label left of the input for the first IPv4 address of the range to allow (prefilled with the blocked IP; label column is narrow).

token_refresh_failed.value: Não foi possível atualizar o token de acesso do Entra: {error}
token_refresh_failed.location: Server Firewall Is Blocking Your IP dialog → Result and Application menu bar → Tools menu → Add My IP to Firewall result window: error detail placed inside the generic failure message when silently renewing the Microsoft Entra access token fails; {error} is the token service error.

validation_ipv4_required.location: Server Firewall Is Blocking Your IP dialog → Status line: red inline error after pressing Add Firewall Rule when Start IP or End IP is not a valid dotted IPv4 address.

validation_name_characters.value: O nome da regra pode conter apenas letras, dígitos, hífens e sublinhados.
validation_name_characters.location: Server Firewall Is Blocking Your IP dialog → Status line: red inline error after pressing Add Firewall Rule when the rule name contains characters other than letters, digits, hyphens or underscores.

validation_name_required.value: Insira um nome para a regra de firewall.
validation_name_required.location: Server Firewall Is Blocking Your IP dialog → Status line: red inline error after pressing Add Firewall Rule with the Rule name field empty.

validation_name_too_long.value: O nome da regra excede o limite de 128 caracteres do Azure.
validation_name_too_long.location: Server Firewall Is Blocking Your IP dialog → Status line: red inline error after pressing Add Firewall Rule when the rule name exceeds Azure’s 128-character limit.

validation_range_order.value: O endereço inicial não pode ser maior que o endereço final.
validation_range_order.location: Server Firewall Is Blocking Your IP dialog → Status line: red inline error after pressing Add Firewall Rule when the Start IP is numerically higher than the End IP.

by_client.location: Workbench → Sidebar → Connections → Group by: full display name of the grouping mode that puts connections into folders by their Client field (the overflow menu currently shows the shorter “By client” label).

by_environment.location: Workbench → Sidebar → Connections → Group by: full display name of the grouping mode that puts connections into folders by environment (Production, Staging and so on); title-case menu-item style.

by_project.location: Workbench → Sidebar → Connections → Group by: full display name of the grouping mode that puts connections into folders by their Project field; title-case menu-item style.

by_server.location: Workbench → Sidebar → Connections → Group by: full display name of the grouping mode that puts connections into folders by server name; title-case menu-item style.

no_grouping.location: Workbench → Sidebar → Connections → Group by: full display name of the default mode that lists connections flat with no group folders (the overflow menu shows it as “All”).

unassigned.location: Workbench → Sidebar → Connections tree: name of the group folder, always sorted last, that collects connections with no value for the active grouping (no client, project, environment or server set).

authenticity_message.value: Não foi possível verificar a autenticidade do host {host}:{port}.
authenticity_message.location: Unknown SSH host key dialog → Body: first line, shown when an SSH tunnel reaches a server whose key is not in known_hosts; {host} is the SSH host name and {port} its port number.

cancel_button.location: Unknown SSH host key dialog → Footer: secondary button that rejects the unfamiliar host key and aborts the SSH tunnel connection.

fingerprint_message.value: A impressão digital da chave {key_type} é SHA256:{fingerprint}
fingerprint_message.location: Unknown SSH host key dialog → Body: second line in monospace under the warning; {key_type} is the key algorithm (for example ssh-ed25519) and {fingerprint} the SHA256 fingerprint to verify.

title.location: Unknown SSH host key dialog → Title bar: dialog title shown when connecting through an SSH tunnel to a host whose key is not yet trusted in known_hosts.

trust_button.location: Unknown SSH host key dialog → Footer: primary button that trusts the shown host key (saving it to known_hosts) and continues the connection.

title.location: SSH verification dialog → Title bar: dialog title shown when an SSH tunnel's server accepted the key or password and now asks for more sign-in information such as a one-time code.

server_message.location: SSH verification dialog → Body: first line naming the SSH account and server that is asking for more sign-in information; {username}, {host} and {port} are the SSH user, server and port.

not_saved_note.value: O que você digita aqui é enviado ao servidor uma vez e nunca é salvo.
not_saved_note.location: SSH verification dialog → Body: small note under the answer fields explaining that the codes typed are sent once and not stored.

continue_button.location: SSH verification dialog → Footer: primary button that sends the typed answers (for example a one-time code) to the SSH server.

cancel_button.location: SSH verification dialog → Footer: secondary button that stops the sign-in without sending any answer; the connection fails.

discovery_failed.location: Connection editor → Routing → Kubernetes port-forward → Status line: error under the section when a Refresh button’s kubectl lookup of contexts, namespaces or targets fails to run; {error} is the system or exit error.

discovery_timed_out.value: A descoberta do Kubernetes expirou após 10 segundos.
discovery_timed_out.location: Connection editor → Routing → Kubernetes port-forward → Status line: error under the section when the kubectl lookup started by a Refresh button gets no answer within 10 seconds.

kubectl_not_found.value: kubectl não foi encontrado no PATH. Instale o kubectl ou defina o caminho dele em Preferências → Avançado → Kubernetes.
kubectl_not_found.location: Connection editor → Routing → Kubernetes port-forward → Status line: dimmed notice under the section, also returned by Refresh, when no kubectl program is on PATH or configured; names the Preferences setting to set it.

account_password_placeholder.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Accounts pane → SQL account details: placeholder in the masked Password input of a saved SQL login account (not the connection form’s password field); a lowercase hint word.

accounts_pane.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Left sidebar: navigation item that opens the Accounts pane, where Microsoft Entra and saved SQL login accounts are managed; short plural noun.

add_connection_status.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Button bar: status text beside the Connect button after the + button clears the form to start a new connection.

add_entra_account_button.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Accounts pane → Account list footer: button that starts a browser sign-in to register a new Microsoft Entra (Azure AD) account.

add_sql_account_button.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Accounts pane → Account list footer: very short button next to the Entra button that clears the details form to create a new saved SQL login account; “+” means add.

advanced_section.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Connection form: heading of the last settings group, holding the connect timeout, query timeout, and startup SQL fields.

appearance_section.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Clients, Projects, and Environments panes → Editor: heading of the group holding the Color picker and Icon drop zone for the selected client, project, or environment.

auth_mode_label.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Connection form → Authentication group: label of the segmented control that picks the sign-in method (SQL login, Windows, Microsoft Entra, IAM, token).

auth_token_hint.value: Cole o token do banco de dados ou o JWT; deixe em branco para um servidor local sem autenticação. Ele é armazenado no chaveiro do sistema.
auth_token_hint.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Connection form → Authentication group: help text under the Auth token field, shown when the engine signs in with a token instead of a username and password.

auth_token_label.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Connection form → Authentication group: label of the masked field for the database access token or JWT, shown for token-based engines.

authentication_section.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Connection form: heading of the settings group that holds the sign-in mode and credential fields.

aws_iam_hint.value: Requer `aws sso login` ou `aws configure`; o token é gerado ao conectar e dura 15 minutos.
aws_iam_hint.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Connection form → Authentication group: help text shown when AWS RDS IAM sign-in is chosen, explaining the required AWS CLI login and the 15-minute token; keep the commands in backticks untranslated.

aws_profile_label.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Connection form → Authentication group: label of the dropdown choosing which local AWS CLI profile mints the RDS IAM token (desktop only).

azure_listing_manual_hint.value: O SQLLY não conseguiu listar seus servidores do Azure SQL — digite o nome do servidor acima.
azure_listing_manual_hint.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Connection form → Server group → Host: note under the Azure server field when SQLLY could not list the account’s Azure SQL servers (often missing permission), telling the user to type the name.

azure_permission_copied.value: Listar servidores exige a função Leitor na assinatura (Microsoft.Sql/servers/read). Uma mensagem para o seu administrador foi copiada para a área de transferência.
azure_permission_copied.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Connection form → Server group → Host: confirmation under the Azure server field after the info button copies a Reader-role request for the user’s admin to the clipboard.

azure_permission_request.value: Você poderia atribuir à minha conta '{account_label}' a função de Leitor na assinatura para que eu possa encontrar os servidores aos quais tenho acesso, em vez de ter que digitá-los manualmente
azure_permission_request.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Azure server field info button: clipboard text copied by the info button beside the Azure server field: a first-person request to an Azure admin asking for the Reader role; {account_label} is the user’s Entra account name.

azure_servers_loading.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Connection form → Server group → Host: loading text inside the Azure SQL server dropdown while the servers for the chosen Microsoft Entra account are fetched.

binding_account_label.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Connections pane → Connection form → Authentication group: small caption above the list of registered Microsoft Entra accounts, shown when Entra sign-in is chosen; the user picks which account to use.

browser_icon_picker_unavailable.value: Não é possível escolher um arquivo de ícone quando o SQLLY roda no navegador
browser_icon_picker_unavailable.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Clients, Projects, and Environments panes → Editor → Footer status: message shown in the browser (web) version when Choose File… is clicked for an icon, because no file picker is available there.

browser_preview_banner.value: Apenas ilustrativo — a visualização web não consegue acessar o SQL Server. Ela roda em um banco de dados de exemplo incluído; use o aplicativo de desktop para se conectar a servidores reais.
browser_preview_banner.location: Connections & Settings dialog → Top banner: notice shown in the browser (web) preview explaining it uses a bundled sample database and cannot reach real SQL Server instances.
